2738.note: The real volume is fr. 3693, not fr. 3689: tome I of 'Ambassade de Mr de Blainville, ambassadeur extraordinaire en Angleterre, 1625 et 1626' (Anc. 9192). The year is 1625, not 1623, and the setting is London. The notice (cc50138c) shows a copy register: 101 items in about 98 folios, several to a leaf. Its headings are quoted from the register: no. 13 'Advis en chiffre, envoie par M. ... evesque de Mande' (on f. 7 with nos. 12 and 14), no. 22 'Advis en chiffre donne a Mr le cardinal de Richelieu ... receu le 26 aoust 1625' (on f. 12 with nos. 20-21), no. 26 'Lettre en chiffre ... receue le 29 aoust 1625' (f. 15). In the comparable Sabran letter-book (fr. 4137, lead 2741, viewed today), the heading 'envoye en chiffre' sits over a clear copy. So these three are most likely clear register copies of avis that had been sent in cipher. Low confidence, since the leaves were not seen.

2745.note: fr. 23202 (Mazarin to the abbe Fouquet, 1651-60) is a run of originals whose cipher passages mostly carry a contemporary interlinear decipherment. Today's views: f. 23r almost fully glossed, f. 23v partly; f. 26r (Sedan, 26 Dec 1651) and f. 28r glossed over nearly every group; another letter at canvas 48 fully glossed. The 15 Nov pass saw the same on canvases 8-9 and 40. A copy of the key is bound at ff. 1-2. Four letters are DECODE records marked solved (R7894-R7897, ff. 67, 279, 306, 350). Chéruel's Lettres de Mazarin IV prints many of these letters, some from clear register copies in Affaires etrangeres, France 268 (e.g. CCXXV f. 21, CCXXXII f. 17). What is left is scattered bare groups (as on f. 23v), a key application with the key in the volume. Not a cryptanalysis target; close it and fold lead 2915 (f. 23) into it.

2747.note: Not assessable from here. The BnF notice of the Noailles papers (cc525100, component d0e2980, per the 16 Nov audit) reads: 'XVIII-XIX Lettres du pere Roslet, minime, au cardinal de Noailles (1700-1713). 223 et 257 feuillets ... en tete du tome I, fol. 1-6, des clefs des chiffres employes'. That establishes the keys, not ciphered letters. It does not say how many letters contain cipher, or whether they were deciphered on receipt. In comparable received runs with the key bound in (Mazarin to Fouquet, fr. 23202, leads 2745/2915), the cipher passages carry interlinear decipherments. Without a view, an open verdict would be a guess. One web search found Roslet's letters to Cardinal Gualterio, 1706-12 (BL Add MS 20398), a possible sibling. It found nothing on a decipherment.

2751.note: The BnF notice (cc40429t) describes NAF 4543 f. 180 as 'Papiers d'Audibert, maitre de musique de l'Academie du roi, a Lyon, relatifs a l'emploi de la notation musicale pour chiffrer les depeches (1746)'. This is a cipher-system proposal filed in Le Dran's 'Memoires musicaux' at the Foreign Affairs depot, not a correspondence. Any specimen in it sits beside the inventor's own explanation of the method, so there is no unread ciphertext to attack. Not seen, so medium confidence. If the papers turn out to hold a specimen without its rule, the lead could be reopened. As a curiosity for the history of music ciphers it is worth a look in the reading room.
